mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, market expectations of future rate hikes diminish, lowering discount rates and boosting the present value of equities, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < mean(FEDFUNDS, lookback=24mo) for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically different from the mean of the 12-month pre-signal period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous 4 months median AND UNRATE < previous 4 months median
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05) relative to the prior 30-day rolling mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above trend for two consecutive months predicts increased near-term business activity and consumer demand, which elevates equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative and remain so across 10 consecutive such signals (rolling mean p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months reduces policy uncertainty and signals disinflation, lowering real discount rates and supporting higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 AND CPIAUCSL < previous 12 months median
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative and statistically indistinguishable from baseline (p > 0.10) during the disflationary window.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of residential mortgage applications (HOUST) exceeds its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months, it indicates renewed housing demand, prompting central banks to be cautious and lowering policy rates expectations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are negative and not statistically different from the prior 60-day mean (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for the first time in 6 months, combined with a continued rise in job openings (PAYEMS), signals a tight labor market that boosts wage growth and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 AND UNRATE < previous 12 months median AND PAYEMS > previous 12 months median
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the tight labor window.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for 4 consecutive months, despite continued economic growth, suggests a structural softening in price pressures that lowers real risk premiums and supports higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 AND CPIAUCSL < previous 12mo median AND CPIAUCSL_trend downward for 4 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are negative and remain so across 5 such episodes (rolling mean p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies; proxy via industrial activity: RSAFS) and a sharp drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two months signals a shift toward sustainable demand without price pressures, which lowers discount rates and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > RSAFS_trend + 1SD AND CPIAUCSL < 2.0 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the demand-led soft landing window.
